```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 4)
library(thermify)
```

## Why densify?

Thermal indices are non-linear in temperature. Applying them to monthly
means biases the result; densifying the monthly normals to daily values
first reduces (but does not remove) that bias, because daily weather
variability is still absent.

## Engines

`densify_monthly()` offers two engines:

* `engine = "tempify"`: the Python package
  [tempify](https://github.com/djwillichile/tempify) through `reticulate`
  (reference implementation, six methods). Data cross the R/Python boundary
  as raw float64 buffers, which avoids any dependence on reticulate's NumPy
  ABI support. The tempify version and git commit are stored in the
  provenance.
* `engine = "native"`: a pure R implementation of `"pchip"` and `"pchip_mp"`
  that reproduces tempify to within 1e-13 degC (tested for 365 and 366 days).

```r
# One-time Python setup (outside R)
# python -m venv ~/.virtualenvs/thermify
# ~/.virtualenvs/thermify/bin/pip install git+https://github.com/djwillichile/tempify
Sys.setenv(RETICULATE_PYTHON = "~/.virtualenvs/thermify/bin/python")
tempify_available()
tempify_version()
```

## The `pchip_mp` algorithm

1. Monthly values are placed at mid-month (day `(days_in_month + 1) %/% 2`).
2. A cyclic PCHIP interpolant (two padding nodes on each side) is evaluated
   for every day.
3. Each month's residual (monthly value minus mean of its daily values) is
   added uniformly to its days. One pass reproduces the monthly mean exactly.

```{r}
tmin <- c(11.4, 11.1, 9.2, 6.8, 5.3, 3.9, 3.1, 3.6, 4.6, 6.3, 8.4, 10.3)
tmax <- c(29.6, 29.2, 26.5, 21.9, 17.2, 13.9, 13.6, 15.3, 17.9, 21.2,
          24.9, 28.2)
mp <- densify_monthly(tmin, tmax, engine = "native", method = "pchip_mp")
pc <- densify_monthly(tmin, tmax, engine = "native", method = "pchip")
plot(mp$dates, mp$tmax[1, ], type = "l", col = "#E8702A", lwd = 2,
     ylab = "Tmax (degC)", xlab = "")
lines(pc$dates, pc$tmax[1, ], col = "grey40", lty = 2)
legend("bottom", c("pchip_mp", "pchip"), col = c("#E8702A", "grey40"),
       lty = 1:2, bty = "n")
rbind(pchip = densify_diagnostics(pc$tmax, tmax, pc$dates),
      pchip_mp = densify_diagnostics(mp$tmax, tmax, mp$dates))
```

Plain PCHIP passes through the mid-month values but does not conserve
monthly means. The uniform correction of `pchip_mp` conserves them exactly
but introduces small steps at month boundaries, reported by
`densify_diagnostics()`. A smoother mean-preserving scheme (full
Rymes & Myers 2001 neighbour smoothing) would remove those steps; this is a
candidate improvement for tempify.

## Physical consistency

`tmin` and `tmax` are densified independently. thermify checks every day for
\(T_{min} \le T_{max}\) and stops if the check fails
(`consistency = "check"`). The alternative `consistency = "mean_range"`
densifies the daily mean and the diurnal range instead; because the
back-transformation is linear, monthly means of both extremes are still
preserved exactly. Extremes are never swapped or clipped silently.
